comments.body:
Progress 2026-08-10 (branch rad-sprint1).

**Done:**
- a_25TdYyCC3 - re-propagated errors name where they re-fired. 68bb2791.
- a_sBQtDAsa - deleting during list iteration no longer duplicates an element. ccc16900. Landed as live+bounds-checked (Python semantics) rather than the snapshot the card leaned toward - snapshotting would have silently killed mid-loop element visibility, a change beyond the bug. See the card.
- a_sBPzQCcM - `?? -1` parses. 9d180293 here, plus 4e554f2 and 649637a upstream. **Not yet landable**: needs the grammar released, now tracked as a_25USSBSSk.

**Left:**
- a_sBQ8LS6p - chained calls. Deliberately not started: the `?? -1` grammar work is still unreleased and `stash@{0}` upstream holds the nested-command WIP, so stacking a third set of `parser.c` regenerations into that tree would entangle all three. Start it from a clean tree after a_25USSBSSk.

Two of the four fixes needed no `rts/` changes at all - the AST, converter, checker and formatter were already general enough. That keeps holding: the chained-call card looks the same way (see its notes).

comments.body: Three of the four have landed on `rad-sprint`: the `?? -1` parse (a_sBPzQCcM), the re-raise attribution (a_25TdYyCC3), and list mutation during iteration (a_sBQtDAsa). Chained calls (a_sBQ8LS6p) are untouched - `make_adder(5)(3)` still errors RAD10009 - so this card stays open on that one alone.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The `bugfixes` board is a separate board from `main`. This card is the pointer so its work does not get lost behind a board you are not looking at this week.

**Restructured 2026-08-10.** This started as "clear the six". Tracing all six to their mechanism showed they were not one unit of work: one was already decided against, and two were the same design question in disguise. What is left here is four code fixes, in dependency order.

| Bug | What it is | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| a_sBPzQCcM | `?? -1` / `catch -1` is a parse error | quick-win, grammar |
| a_25TdYyCC3 | Re-propagated errors are blamed on the original call site | |
| a_sBQtDAsa | Mutating a list while iterating skips elements | design |
| a_sBQ8LS6p | No chained-call syntax - `make_adder(5)(3)` is a parse error | grammar |

**Lifted off this card:**
- a_sBR0JLWj (nested loops clobber the outer var) - **closed as a duplicate of a_sBRVjVvW.** Same code path, and a_sBRVjVvW was already closed works-as-intended: loops do not open scopes (docs/type_system.md:129-133), and scoping.snap:30-59 asserts loop vars persist. Fixing it is option (B) from that card, explicitly rejected. See the comment there.
- a_sBQgqO7u and a_sBRDpFgU (design halves) - **blocked on a_25TdzYuMr**, "does an error value stay armed once bound to a variable". One question, one RED, not two bugfixes.

---

### Order, and why

**First: a_sBPzQCcM.** Not because it is the smallest change - it is not, any grammar edit is a multi-repo release - but because it forces us through that entire loop on a trivially-correct change before a_sBQ8LS6p depends on it working.

**Then: a_25TdYyCC3.** Contained, in `core/`, and independent of the error-identity decision.

**Then: a_sBQtDAsa.** One sub-choice, with an obvious lean - see the card.

**Last: a_sBQ8LS6p.** Cheaper than it looks. The AST and interpreter already support chained calls; only the grammar refuses. See the card.

### Orientation

- Two of the four are grammar gaps in the separate `amterp/tree-sitter-rad` repo, reached here through `rts/`.
- `rts/` owns CST-to-AST conversion (`rts/converter.go`), the AST (`rts/rl/`), the checker (`rts/check/`) and the formatter (`rts/radfmt/`). A grammar change means editing the grammar upstream, bumping `github.com/amterp/tree-sitter-rad` in `go.mod` (currently v0.6.0), and handling the new node shape in `rts/converter.go`. `rts` must not import `core`.
- `radls/` inherits grammar and checker changes for free through `rts/`, but `rts/radfmt/` needs a print rule for any new syntax.
- Checkouts for the first-party deps live at `~/src/tree-sitter-rad` and `~/src/ra`. Iterate with a local `replace` directive in `go.mod` and remove it before committing - `./dev --release` refuses to release with one present.

### Watch out for

- **Re-verify every repro against the current build first.** The cards were last verified on v0.10.1 on 2026-06-14; we are on v0.11.0, which carries the `+=` fix (117b7329). The map half of a_sBQtDAsa already silently stopped reproducing once - that is the failure mode to guard against.
- The bugfixes cards carry repros, re-verification dates, and root-cause notes. They do not carry file:line fix pointers; each card now has one where I found it.

### Related

GitHub #140 proposes a property-based test harness for exactly this class of bug, with metamorphic oracles (inlining a call must not change output; an unused local must change nothing). Now tracked as a_25TeTnRDT in p2. Not a gate on this work, but it is the only cheap way to prove the a_25TdzYuMr decision holds at depth.
title: Clear the four shippable todo-hi bugs on the bugfixes board
